messages:
maya_cs: Heads up — renewal for Hightower is coming due 2026-04-10. Procurement sent back a special request: they need two invoices (US entity + EU entity), ACH only, and net-90 terms. Also asking that the Dedicated capacity SOW be attached as a separate exhibit. Can we accept net-90 + split invoice?

tom_ae: thanks Maya. Their legal contact flagged the EU signer needs to sign under the EU entity (different PO). They also want our KMS clause removed for the EU part.

alex_legal: Removing KMS clause for a sub-entity is a no-go without approvals — need risk signoff. Also net-90 is a credit decision with finance. We can draft an exhibit for the SOW but need to be explicit about which entity is liable.

sanjay_finance: Net-90 and ACH-only is high risk for us given customer history. We can consider a conditional approval if we get an advance partial payment (30%) or a revenue assurance clause. Also need the vendor GL code to map invoices.

maya_cs: Procurement asked for a single vendor code per invoice — they can't accept combined lines. They want us to add invoice footer with "PO: 2026-HIGHT-RENEW" for both docs.

julie_pm: For the Dedicated SOW: we have a template. I'll attach the exhibit draft to the contract branch and label it Exhibit A - Dedicated (EU) and Exhibit B - Dedicated (US). Any redlines?

alex_legal: Draft looked at quick pass — two asks: 1) make EU exhibit GDPR-compliant language explicit, 2) include a fallback for support latency SLAs tied to region. I'll add comments.

tom_ae: Customer is asking for a 15% one-time discount if they sign both entities together and commit to a 12‑month term. If we push partial payment + 12mo term, that might be acceptable.

sanjay_finance: 15% one-time discount is okay if we get the 30% upfront and ACH transfer confirmed. Approve contingent on escrow for the EU invoice until payment clears.

maya_cs: Action items: @tom_ae to confirm customer's willingness to 30% upfront; @julie_pm to create separate exhibits; @alex_legal to add GDPR and SLA fallbacks; @sanjay_finance to draft payment guard language. Deadline: need signoff by 2026-04-02 to hit renewal date.

tom_ae: pinging customer now — will push 30% upfront + 12mo + accept split invoices.

docusign-bot: Document created: Renewal_Hightower_2026_v3.pdf — exhibit placeholders inserted.

maya_cs: Perfect. Keep updates here. If customer refuses upfront we should prepare a 60-day extension playbook and a one-time pragmatic credit instead of 15% discount.

julie_pm: Uploaded Exhibit_A_EU_draft.pdf and Exhibit_B_US_draft.pdf to the contract branch: link: https://redwood.internal/contracts/HIGHTOWER/renewal-2026

tom_ae: Customer replied — they can do 15% + 12mo, but only 45 days upfront, not 30%. Asking if we can change to 45 days and ACH after invoice generation.

sanjay_finance: 45 days is closer to net-45 territory; still risky but acceptable if we hold the EU invoice in escrow for 30 days post-issue. I'll draft escrow clause.

alex_legal: I'll add escrow and ensure the EU exhibit has the signature block separated. Also will add the language: "Signature by EU entity binds only EU exhibit".

maya_cs: Cool — next steps: finalize contract edits, get legal/finance sign-off, then send split docusign flows (separate sign requests to US and EU signers). Aim to send by 2026-03-30.

tom_ae: noted — I'll schedule the sends and coordinate signing windows with the customer (they're in CET).

maya_cs: Thanks team. I'll prepare a short enablement note for onboarding: mention dual-entity billing, contact routing for EU support, and dedicated SOW differences. Will drop that once contract is final. :thumbsup:
